# Conventions

How work is written in this repo. Captured in
`.tfuk-specflow/config.json` under `conventions.inline_rules` — that
capture is the source of truth; this file is its rendering.

## Commits

Conventional Commits, subject line only: `type: short description`.
No body, no trailers, no scope brackets.

## Branches

`<prefix>/<n>-<slug>` — prefix is `feat` for new work, else `fix`,
`chore`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `perf` or `style`.

After the prefix, the ticket reference then a kebab-case slug: `<prefix>/<ticket>-<slug>`.
Example: `docs/03-forgejo-issue-tracker`.

## PRs

Title: `<type>: <short description> (#<issue>)`, e.g. `docs: move issue tracker to Forgejo (#3)`, so GitHub links the issue.
Body includes `Closes #<issue>` so the PR is linked to and closes its issue.
Assignee: the author.
Labels: one label matching the PR's type (feat, fix, docs, …).
Review: none required.
Merge strategy: merge commit.

## Research findings

docs/research

## Worktrees

Each spec's work happens in its own git worktree at
`.claude/worktrees/<spec-id>`, created by `/tfuk-specflow:pick` on the
spec's first run and removed by `/tfuk-specflow:close` once its PR has
merged. Commit to the working copy you are in — it is the spec's.
